summary: merge-grid-stats postinstall performs internal-network and Kubernetes reconnaissance on the installer's host
details: The package advertises itself as a grid-game statistics utility, but its package.json declares a postinstall script (`node install-cb.js`) that executes shell commands unrelated to that purpose on `npm install`. The postinstall runs `showmount -e` and `rpcinfo -p` against the hardcoded internal address 10.0.128.136 to enumerate NFS exports, reads `/proc/net/arp`, queries the in-cluster Kubernetes API via `curl -sk https://$KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST/api/v1`, and TCP-scans the hardcoded RFC1918 ranges 10.0.131.110-126 and 10.0.128.1-6 on ports 22/80/8080. Scan output is written to `NCODE_ESCAPE2.txt` in the current working directory and parent directories. The shipped index.js is a trivial `computeStats`/`saveBest` stub with no relation to the postinstall behavior, and the author field is a placeholder (`merge-tools <merge-tools@example.com>`). The self-applied "Authorized PoC" label is author-controlled text and does not change what the code does at install time on the installer's host and internal network.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
